hook: Hoffman co-founded LinkedIn in 2002 and later became a partner at Greylock in 2009. He was a financial backer named in OpenAI's founding announcement in December 2015, later joined OpenAI's board in 2018, and left that board in March 2023. In 2022 he co-founded Inflection AI with Mustafa Suleyman and Karen Simonyan.

reading.body:
Reid Hoffman has positioned himself across the full cycle of AI capital formation, from early backing of OpenAI in 2015 through founding a competing AI company in 2022, while maintaining influence as a venture investor at Greylock since 2009.

His trajectory shows a pattern common among technology investors: build a large-scale platform, translate that success into venture capital authority, then deploy that authority into the next wave of technology. LinkedIn's billion-member network gave Hoffman both capital and credibility. Greylock formalized his role as a backer of early-stage companies. His presence in OpenAI's founding announcement in December 2015 placed him at the moment the modern AI race began.

The data reveals a deliberate move toward concentration of influence. Hoffman joined OpenAI's board in 2018 and remained there until March 2023, when he resigned citing conflicts among his AI-related investments and roles. Within a year of that resignation, the conflict became concrete: he had co-founded Inflection AI in March 2022, months before leaving OpenAI's board. This sequence shows how a single investor can fund and direct multiple AI companies simultaneously, and why he felt compelled to step back from OpenAI governance to do so.

What this does not reveal is the scale of capital deployed, the computational resources Inflection AI commands, or how Hoffman's Greylock investments intersect with the power and infrastructure constraints that govern AI scaling. His influence is documented as organizational and financial, not as direct access to the buildings and electricity that compute requires.

standing.watch: What remains unresolved in the records is the litigation. Every case listed is filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet by this tracker, so no outcome, ruling, or settlement appears for any of them. The OpenAI cases and the Anthropic case carry dates in 2026 for Bass, United States v. OpenAI OpCo LLC, GRANT, Smigelski, and JIANG, while USA Today Co. and TradeSun carry no date in the records. Nothing in the records states a pending listing, a planned financing, or a dispute involving Hoffman personally. Where the records are thin, they say only that these matters are filed and being monitored.
standing.record: The site's records place Hoffman at the center of four companies: Greylock Partners, where he is listed as an executive of an investor founded in 1965; Inflection AI, which he founded in 2022 in Palo Alto; LinkedIn, which he founded and which is listed as a startup founded in 2003 in Sunnyvale; and OpenAI, in which he invested and which was founded in 2015 in San Francisco. The lawsuits on the site do not name Hoffman. They name OpenAI entities in USA Today Co., Inc. v. OpenAI Foundation, TradeSun, Inc. v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, Bass v. OpenAI, LLC, United States v. OpenAI OpCo LLC, GRANT v. OPENAI INC, Smigelski v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, and JIANG v. OPENAI GROUP PBC, and they name Anthropic in Buist v. Anthropic, PBC. Each is recorded as filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet by this tracker. The pattern is a portfolio and founding record in AI and venture investing, with the litigation concentrated on OpenAI rather than on Hoffman himself.
standing.standing: Reid Hoffman stands in artificial intelligence as a co-founder of Inflection AI, a partner at Greylock, and a named financial backer of OpenAI, according to the records. He co-founded Inflection AI in 2022 with Mustafa Suleyman and Karen Simonyan, and he has been a partner at Greylock since 2009. His OpenAI connection runs from the December 2015 founding announcement, where he was named as a financial backer, to a board seat he joined in 2018 and left in March 2023. He also co-founded LinkedIn, which the records date to 2002 in the profile and 2003 in the quick facts.
